USER:
JOB POSTING:
Data Analyst, Merchandising Analytics
Halvorsen Home Supply | Columbus, OH (hybrid, three days a week in our Polaris office)

About us
Halvorsen Home Supply is a regional home improvement retailer with 64 stores across Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and western Pennsylvania, plus a growing online business. Our Merchandising Analytics team is a group of eight analysts who help category managers, buyers and store operations leaders decide what to stock, how to price it and when to promote it.

The role
We are hiring a Data Analyst to own weekly sales, margin and inventory reporting for two of our largest departments, building materials and seasonal. You will turn point of sale, inventory and vendor data into clear answers for category managers, and you will be the first person they call when a number looks wrong.

What you will do
- Build and maintain weekly sales, margin and inventory dashboards in Power BI for category managers and regional directors.
- Write SQL against our Snowflake data warehouse to answer ad hoc questions about product, store and promotion performance.
- Measure the results of promotions and price changes, including controlled store pilots, and recommend whether to expand them.
- Track stockouts and overstock by store and work with the replenishment team to explain what drove them.
- Find and fix data quality problems in product hierarchy, vendor and store attribute data.
- Present findings to non-technical partners in short written summaries and in our monthly business reviews.

What we are looking for
- Three or more years of experience in a data analyst, reporting analyst or similar role.
- Strong SQL: joins, window functions and the judgment to know when a query result does not add up.
- Advanced Excel and hands-on experience with a BI tool (Power BI preferred, Tableau or Looker welcome).
- A bachelor's degree in statistics, economics, mathematics, computer science or a related quantitative field.
- Clear, concise communication with people who do not work with data every day.

Nice to have
- Python or R for analysis and automation.
- Experience with retail, distribution or supply chain data.
- Familiarity with Snowflake or another cloud data warehouse.

What we offer
- Salary range of $72,000 to $88,000, plus an annual bonus.
- Medical, dental and vision coverage, a 401(k) with a 5 percent match and an employee discount.
- Fifteen days of paid time off in your first year, plus paid holidays.

APPLICATION:
Latasha Burke
Columbus, OH | (614) 555-0123 | latasha.burke@gmail.com

SUMMARY
Analyst at a nonprofit research center with seven years of applied quantitative work for government and operational clients. Writes some SQL in PostgreSQL, analyzes survey and transaction data in R, and turns results into short findings that program managers act on. Recent work has moved from survey reporting toward operational analysis of ridership and service data, and the next step is a business analytics team.

EXPERIENCE
Survey Analyst | Hollister Center for Public Policy Research, Columbus, OH | Jul 2021 to Present
• Manage data analysis for four to six concurrent client projects a year for state agencies, including a transit rider study, a workforce training follow-up and a licensing board customer satisfaction survey.
• Produced boardings tables by route and hour from fare card transactions for a regional transit authority study, working from query templates written by the project director.
• Help maintain the center's PostgreSQL project database, writing joins that link survey responses to client administrative records.
• Update a basic Tableau view of weekly complaint volume by route for the transit study team.
• Check incoming fare card and complaint extracts against the prior month for missing days or unexpected jumps in record counts before the files are loaded, and send the data provider a short note when something looks off.
• Tabulated response rates for a mailed versus text message invitation pilot in the workforce study for the project director's memo.
• Wrote reusable R scripts for cleaning Qualtrics exports and producing crosstabs, which shortened report preparation on a typical project.
• Build sampling frames and weights in R and SPSS so results match the populations each client serves.
• Meet with client project managers at kickoff and at each interim report to agree on scope, sample sizes and deadlines, and write short findings memos alongside the full report.

Research Assistant | Hollister Center for Public Policy Research, Columbus, OH | Jun 2019 to Jun 2021
• Supported three project directors on studies for state health and transportation agencies, preparing data files and draft tables for each interim deliverable.
• Cleaned and merged administrative data files in SPSS, documenting every recode in a project codebook.
• Ran descriptive statistics and regression models and built the tables and charts for interim reports.
• Coordinated phone survey fieldwork with an outside call center, tracking daily completes against quotas in Excel and sending a short status note to the project director each afternoon.
• Built a small Shiny app in R so project leads could check response rates by region during fieldwork.
• Checked agency administrative files against survey sample lists and flagged about 1,200 records with outdated addresses before a mail wave.

EDUCATION
Bachelor of Science in Statistics, The Ohio State University, 2019

SKILLS
Data: SQL in PostgreSQL (joins, aggregation), Excel (pivot tables, lookups, Power Query)
Analysis: R (tidyverse, survey, Shiny), SPSS, regression, sampling and weighting
Reporting: Tableau Desktop, ggplot2 charts, short findings memos and slide summaries
Survey tools: Qualtrics, REDCap, questionnaire design

ADDITIONAL
• Completed an intermediate SQL course on window functions and query tuning, 2026
• Volunteer survey design help for a Columbus neighborhood association's annual resident survey
